overview: Council President Zac Bears discussed Medford's long-term financial strategy, the progress of the high school building project, and the need for commercial growth to stabilize the residential tax base. He also addressed public engagement challenges and his vision for zoning and infrastructure improvements.

items.title: Personal Background and Legislative Philosophy
items.summary: Zac Bears described himself as a Medford native and principled advocate who bases his council work on transparency and data-driven policy.

items.title: Budget Process and 2024 Override Impacts
items.summary: Bears highlighted a more collaborative budget process with the Mayor and the successful negotiation of a new teacher contract following the 2024 tax override votes.

items.title: Infrastructure and DPW Capacity
items.summary: The discussion identified the failure to execute existing plans and a significant backlog in road and sidewalk maintenance as major ongoing challenges for the city.

items.title: Public Engagement and Public Discourse
items.summary: Bears reflected on the tension surrounding recent zoning debates, acknowledging the need for the council to improve communication and lower the temperature of public disagreements.

items.title: Commercial Growth and Tax Revenue
items.summary: Bears advocated for attracting walkable, mixed-use commercial development in city squares to diversify the tax base and reduce the burden on homeowners.

items.title: Housing Policy and Zoning Reform
items.summary: Bears proposed a "City of Yes" approach to zoning that allows homeowners more flexibility to adapt their property while pursuing bold development projects in commercial corridors.

items.title: Medford High School and Fire Station Projects
items.summary: Bears reviewed the MSBA timeline for the high school building project and characterized the failed 2024 fire station debt exclusion as a missed opportunity to address end-of-life facilities.

items.title: Long-Term Vision for Medford
items.summary: Bears outlined a 15-year vision for the city focused on safe streets for all transit modes, expanded housing options, and a proactive mindset toward development at City Hall.
